summary: Oldřich Hujer was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and studied at Leipzig under August Leskien. He taught at Charles University from 1911, serving as ordinary professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics (1924–1942).

Ole Holten Pind worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner (circa 2003–2009) and later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar was an art historian who studied at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (PhD circa 1950–1955). He held professorships at the University of Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard University (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).
Olha Dobrodum is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Odesa University in 2015 and held a post at the State University of Trade and Economics.

Oliver Codrington was an Indologist and medical doctor educated at the London Hospital. He served as deputy surgeon-general in the Army Medical Department (1859–1885) and as librarian for the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (1891–1919/1921).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede, he became Head of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon in 1943 and was a guest professor at Pennsylvania in 1963.

Oliver Hellwig works in Indology, computational linguistics, and linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and has held posts at the University of Düsseldorf and the University of Zurich (attested 2024–2025).
Oliver Petersen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang (circa 1983–2003) and held a post at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (attested 2002).

Oliver Philipp Frey is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Vienna, where he was a predoc assistant (2013–2016). He held an SNSF Postdoc.Mobility Fellowship at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2023–2025).
Olivia Porter works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at King's College London until 2023 and became a teaching fellow at the University of Leeds in 2025.

Olivier Lacombe studied philosophy, Indology, and religious studies at the École Normale Supérieure and Faculty of Arts of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Masson-Oursel. He was a professor at Ankara, Lille, EPHE, and the University of Paris.

Olivier de Bernon is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He has held positions at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (circa 1991) and as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Olle Qvarnström is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Lund University under Tord Olsson, as well as at Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen. He held an editorial post as ansvarig utgivare at Lund University (attested 2000–2007).
Olli Littunen is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a BA at Leiden University (2016–2022) and undertook doctoral research under Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Olof August Danielsson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch. At Uppsala, he served as docent (1879), professor of comparative linguistics (1883), and professor of Greek language and literature (1891).

Om Prakash is an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. He taught at Delhi University, Kirori Mal College, and was a professor of economic history at the Delhi School of Economics.

On Shionoya was a Sinologist who completed studies at Tokyo Imperial University (circa 1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (circa 1912–1914). He later held a faculty post at Tokyo Imperial University from circa 1920 to 1939.
Ondřej Novák was an Indologist and historian who studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. there between circa 1964 and 1975.

Onorio Ferrero de Gubernatis Ventimiglia was a scholar in Indology. He taught Oriental languages and cultures at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru (1952–1976) and at the National University of San Marcos.

Oreste Nazari was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied under Gaspare Gorresio. He was a teacher at the University of Turin (circa 1898–1923) and served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Palermo from 1901 to 1923.
